This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment
1.
Being dissatisfied with the award of compensation of Rs.1,08,500/-, the claimant is in this appeal seeking enhancement.
2. The occurrence of the accident and the liability to pay compensation by the Insurer are not in dispute.
3. The Tribunal has come to the conclusion that P.W.4 was examined and he had stated that on a medical examination of the claimant, he was found to be normal.
The Tribunal has also noticed that the claimant was examined as P.W.1 and he has successfully withstood.
In the cross-examination and NC: 2024:KHC:45617 he had given perfect answers and therefore, the medical evidence that he had certain effects due to head injury cannot be accepted.

In my view, this finding of the Tribunal that the claimant had recovered from his injuries cannot be found fault with and, therefore, refusal to award any compensation towards 'loss of future earnings' cannot be found fault with.
4. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- each towards 'pain and sufferings' and 'loss of amenities'.

Since the evidence on record indicates that claimant had suffered a head injury and was hospitalized for 12 days in five different hospitals, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.50,000/- towards 'loss of amenities.
5. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as two months.

In my view, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as four months and having regard NC: 2024:KHC:45617 to the fact that the accident was of the year 2015, the notional income as determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is Rs.9,000/-.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled to Rs.36,000/- (Rs.9,000/- x 4 S Chandan vs Smt. Munirathnamma on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169037305/
2 months).

6. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards 'conveyance and diet' and the same is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-, in view of the fact that claimant is hospitalsed for 12 days.

7. As regards Rs.14,500/- awarded towards 'medical expenses', Rs.10,000/- awarded towards 'future medical expenditure', and Rs.20,000/- awarded towards 'physical impairment' in my view, the same are just and proper and are accordingly affirmed.
8. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

9. As far as liability is concerned, the Tribunal has exonerated the insurer of all liability on the ground that the validity of the registration of the insured vehicle had expired.
It is not in dispute that the insurer had insured the vehicle as on the date of the accident.

The question as to whether the S Chandan vs Smt. Munirathnamma on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169037305/
3 vehicle NC: 2024:KHC:45617 registration had expired or not would have no relevance insofar as the liability of the insurer is concerned.
If the registration of the vehicle had expired, the owner of the vehicle would suffer a liability to pay the penalty.
But, so long as the insurer had issued a policy covering its use as a motor vehicle, the insurer cannot escape its liability.
Consequently, the finding with regard to exonerating the insurer is set aside and the insurer is held to be liable to pay the compensation.
10. Accordingly, the claimant is held entitled to a compensation of Rs.2,25,500/- as against Rs.1,08,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
11. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The other aspects of the Award of the Tribunal remain undisturbed.
13. This appeal is, accordingly, allowed in part.
